youtube.title: Blockbuster, the $50 Million Netflix Offer, and the Fight After
youtube.description:
In 2000, Netflix offered itself to Blockbuster for $50 million and was turned down. Ten years later Blockbuster was bankrupt and Netflix was on its way to $39 billion a year. The popular story is that one 'no' killed Blockbuster. A later Blockbuster CEO says Netflix did not kill it.

This documentary follows the decision that really shaped the end: fighting Netflix by giving up late fees and building online, on a balance sheet already carrying the debt from a 2004 dividend. Then the board fight, the cuts, and the collapse. Every figure on screen is from filings, books and named reports.

{CHAPTERS}

youtube.comment: Was Blockbuster's real mistake in 2000, in 2004 or in 2007? 👇

sources.claim: The store in Bend, Oregon has been the last Blockbuster since 2019, after a store in Australia closed
sources.source: Associated Press, 'World's last Blockbuster in Oregon', March 2019

sources.claim: Blockbuster filed for Chapter 11 on September 23, 2010, listing about $1.46 billion in liabilities
sources.source: Blockbuster Inc. voluntary petition, US Bankruptcy Court SDNY, 23 Sep 2010; Reuters, 23 Sep 2010

sources.claim: In 2000 Netflix offered itself to Blockbuster for $50 million
'Netflix did not kill Blockbuster' (Jim Keyes)
sources.source: Fortune, interview with former Blockbuster CEO Jim Keyes, March 2024

sources.claim: Blockbuster opened its first store in Dallas in 1985
sources.source: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K, company history; New York Times, 1994 coverage of Viacom deal

sources.claim: Viacom agreed to buy Blockbuster for $8.4 billion in 1994
About 9,000 Blockbuster stores worldwide in 2004
Blockbuster revenue about $6 billion in 2004
Netflix was founded in 1997
Reed Hastings says a $40 late fee for Apollo 13 gave him the idea
sources.source: Reed Hastings and Erin Meyer, 'No Rules Rules' (2020)

sources.claim: Marc Randolph wrote that the late-fee story was not how Netflix began
In 1999 Netflix moved to a monthly subscription with no due dates or late fees
Netflix lost about $57 million in 2000 on revenue of about $36 million
Netflix had about 292,000 subscribers at the end of 2000
Hastings, Randolph and Netflix's finance chief met Blockbuster CEO John Antioco and his general counsel in Dallas
Netflix proposed running Blockbuster's brand online while Blockbuster promoted Netflix in stores
'Antioco was struggling not to laugh.'
Blockbuster revenue about $5 billion in 2000
The $50 million offer was about one percent of Blockbuster's 2000 revenue
sources.source: Calculated from Randolph (2019) and Blockbuster Form 10-K, fiscal 2000

sources.claim: Blockbuster and Enron announced a 20-year movies-on-demand deal in July 2000
sources.source: Blockbuster/Enron joint announcement, 19 Jul 2000; Wall Street Journal, July 2000

sources.claim: The Blockbuster-Enron deal ended in March 2001
Netflix went public in May 2002
Netflix had about 2.6 million subscribers at the end of 2004, about 4.2 million at the end of 2005 and about 6.3 million at the end of 2006
Viacom completed its split-off from Blockbuster in October 2004
Before the 2004 Viacom split-off, Blockbuster paid a $5-a-share special dividend of about $905 million, funded with borrowing; Viacom was the majority shareholder
Blockbuster still carried long-term debt at the end of 2006
Blockbuster launched its own online rental service in 2004
Blockbuster announced on 14 Dec 2004 that late fees would end from 1 Jan 2005; films kept a week past due were charged at sale price minus the rental
sources.source: Blockbuster press release, 14 Dec 2004; New York Times, Dec 2004

sources.claim: New Jersey sued over the 'no late fees' advertising in 2005; Blockbuster settled with 47 states for about $630,000
sources.source: New Jersey Attorney General, January 2005; Associated Press, March 2005

sources.claim: Carl Icahn won three Blockbuster board seats in a proxy fight in May 2005
sources.source: Harvard Business Review, Antioco, April 2011; New York Times, May 2005

sources.claim: In Antioco's account the board questioned the online spending and disputed his pay
sources.source: John Antioco, 'How I Did It: Blockbuster's Former CEO on Sparring with an Activist Shareholder', Harvard Business Review, April 2011

sources.claim: Total Access launched in November 2006, letting online renters return discs in stores for a free rental
Blockbuster's online service passed two million subscribers in early 2007
Antioco later put the total cost at about $400 million: $200 million in lost late fees and $200 million to build online
sources.source: John Antioco, Harvard Business Review, April 2011

sources.claim: Antioco left in 2007; Jim Keyes, former 7-Eleven CEO, became chief executive in July 2007
Total Access prices rose and its marketing was cut under the new management
Netflix began streaming films to computers at no extra charge in January 2007
Redbox kiosks rented DVDs for one dollar a night
sources.source: New York Times, 2009 coverage of Redbox

sources.claim: Blockbuster offered about $1 billion for Circuit City in April 2008 and withdrew in July 2008
'Neither RedBox nor Netflix are even on the radar screen in terms of competition.' (Jim Keyes)
sources.source: The Motley Fool, interview with Jim Keyes, December 2008

sources.claim: In 2009 Blockbuster's revenue fell by more than $1 billion
sources.source: Calculated from Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal 2008 and 2009 ($5.29B to $4.06B)

sources.claim: In September 2009 Blockbuster said it would close up to 960 stores
In October 2009 Blockbuster raised about $675 million in senior secured notes to refinance its loans
sources.source: Reuters, September-October 2009; Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal 2009

sources.claim: In March 2010 Blockbuster's annual report raised substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern
sources.source: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal 2009, filed March 2010; Reuters, March 2010

sources.claim: Blockbuster shares were removed from the New York Stock Exchange in July 2010
Dish Network bought Blockbuster at auction in April 2011 for about $320 million
In November 2013 Dish said it would close its last 300 company-owned stores, affecting about 2,800 jobs
Netflix reported about $39 billion in revenue for 2024
A Kodak engineer built a digital camera in 1975
sources.source: Kodak corporate history; New York Times, 2015 profile of engineer Steven Sasson
